questions.question_text: A Rhode Island agent posts a property listing on social media without including any brokerage name. What violation has occurred?
distractors: Violating fair housing rules
Failing to disclose agency
Advertising without MLS approval
questions.explanation: Every advertisement must carry the name of the brokerage or principal broker, displayed larger and more prominent than any licensee or team name (230-RICR-30-20-2.25(C)). On social media the brokerage name must be within one click or tap of the post.

questions.question_text: Agent Kim operates on a team called 'Kim's Elite Homes.' Her team's flyer lists only the team name. What must be added to comply with RI advertising rules?
distractors: Kim's personal license number
The team's direct phone number
The property MLS listing number
questions.explanation: Team names are allowed, but the brokerage name must appear and be larger and more prominent (230-RICR-30-20-2.25(C)). A team name must also include the word 'Team' or 'Group,' so 'Kim's Elite Homes' falls short on that count too.

questions.question_text: Which statement about Rhode Island advertising rules is correct?
questions.correct_answer: Internet ads follow the same rules as print ads
distractors: Social media posts are exempt from disclosure
Team names may replace the brokerage name
Broker name is optional on yard signs
questions.explanation: Internet and social media advertising carry the same identification duty as print. The brokerage name and contact information must appear on the home page and every viewable page, and within one click or tap of any character-limited post (230-RICR-30-20-2.25(E)).

questions.question_text: A broker's website features testimonials claiming guaranteed returns on investment properties. Which rule does this violate?
questions.correct_answer: Ban on misleading or deceptive ads
distractors: Blind advertising prohibition rule
Team name disclosure requirement
Escrow account handling regulations
questions.explanation: A licensee shall not advertise in any way that is false or misleading (230-RICR-30-20-2.25(B)). Guaranteeing investment returns is inherently misleading, because the outcome is not something the brokerage can promise.

questions.question_text: A yard sign shows the agent's name in large lettering with the brokerage name in small print underneath. What is wrong with it?
questions.correct_answer: The brokerage name must be the larger of the two
distractors: Nothing, as long as both names appear
Yard signs may not carry an agent's name at all
The agent's license number is missing
questions.explanation: In all print media the brokerage's information must be in a font size larger than any licensee or team name, and at least as visible (230-RICR-30-20-2.25(D)). Business cards are the one exception to the smaller-print rule.

questions.question_text: A listing agent offers a seller's neighbor $500 for referring the neighbor's coworker as a buyer. The neighbor is unlicensed. Is this permitted?
questions.correct_answer: No, paying unlicensed persons is prohibited
distractors: Yes, if the total amount is under $1,000
Yes, if the managing broker approves it
Yes, if disclosed to all parties involved
questions.explanation: Paying any part of a commission to a person who is not licensed but who by law should be is an express ground for discipline (§ 5-20.5-14(31)). The amount paid and any disclosure make no difference.

questions.question_text: Agent Rivera tells a seller that the home will sell for $50,000 above market value to secure the listing. What violation is this?
distractors: Failure to present all offers
Breach of fiduciary duty only
Violation of escrow fund regulations
questions.explanation: Making substantial misrepresentations or false promises is grounds for disciplinary action in Rhode Island. Intentionally inflating an expected sale price to obtain a listing constitutes a false promise and is a prohibited act.

questions.question_text: An agent represents both the buyer and seller but does not inform either party about the dual relationship. Which requirement was violated?
distractors: Advertising identification rules
Continuing education mandate
Escrow deposit timeline
questions.explanation: A licensee must disclose any interest in the transaction in writing at the first point of personal contact, and no later than making an offer to purchase (230-RICR-30-20-2.21(G)). Serving both sides without disclosure and consent breaches that duty.

questions.question_text: A buyer's agent learns the property has a history of flooding but decides not to mention it because the seller's disclosure was silent on the issue. What is the agent's obligation?
questions.correct_answer: Disclose all material facts to all parties
distractors: Rely solely on the seller's disclosure form
Disclose the flooding only if asked directly
Report the issue only to the listing agent
questions.explanation: Licensees must make a diligent effort to ascertain pertinent facts and reveal in writing all information material to the transaction (230-RICR-30-20-2.22(B)). A known flooding history is material regardless of what the seller's form says.

questions.question_text: Which marketing tactic is an express ground for discipline under Rhode Island's license law?
questions.correct_answer: Running a prize drawing to attract prospective buyers
distractors: Offering a seller a reduced commission rate
Preparing a detailed comparative market analysis
Advertising a listing across several platforms
questions.explanation: Soliciting or offering real property by giving away free lots, running lotteries or contests, or offering prizes to influence a purchaser or prospective purchaser is a ground for discipline (§ 5-20.5-14(18)).
